## Llanos Lab – Research Assistant					      

**Columbia University, Mailman School of Public Health, Department of Epidemiology; New York, NY; January 2026 – Present; The ACHIEVE Study - Research Assistant**

* Evaluate the association of social and structural factors on receipt of guideline-concordant care for invasive cervical cancer
Evaluate the association of social and structural factors on cervical cancer outcomes
* Identify actionable strategies for addressing social and structural risks and health system-level factors to optimize delivery of equitable cervical cancer care through participatory engagement of stakeholders
* Complete data entry of baseline and 12-month follow-up surveys of cervical cancer participants into a database (REDCap) that translates answers into statistical findings
* Create a literature review and data analysis on the association between patient-provider racial, ethnic, and gender concordance and patient-provider communication during cervical cancer treatment, through previous publications
